digest.headline: August US payrolls dragged stocks lower while Japan saw a yen surge and China injected $54 billion into lenders.

lede.b: Strong US payroll data for August pushed the S&P 500 and the Dow lower. Payroll data counts how many people have jobs. When employment is hot, investors worry that the Federal Reserve — the central bank that sets official borrowing costs in the United States — will raise interest rates to slow the economy down. Higher interest rates make borrowing more expensive for companies and consumers. At the same time, the Japanese yen surged by 2.0% after a central bank official made unexpected remarks, which caused investors to unwind speculative trades. China also injected $54 billion into major lenders and insurers to offset deflationary pressures.
lede.i: Hot August payrolls dragged the S&P 500 and the Dow lower as strong labor data increased expectations that the Federal Reserve might implement further rate hikes. Bond yields reacted to the employment figures by shifting rate probability pricing across portfolios. In Japan, the currency rallied 2.0% following unexpected remarks from a Bank of Japan official, triggering a rapid unwinding of the yen carry trade. Meanwhile, state authorities in China injected $54 billion into major lenders and insurers to combat deflation.
lede.a: Hot August payroll prints compressed the S&P 500 and the Dow as front-end rate probability pricing adjusted for potential Federal Reserve tightening. Concurrently, a hawkish surprise from a Bank of Japan official sparked a 2.0% yen rally, accelerating a liquidation of the carry trade across global forex desks. In Asia, Chinese authorities injected $54 billion of liquidity into systemic lenders and insurers to mitigate persistent deflationary impulses.

thread.b: Global markets reacted to shifting employment data from the United States. Central banks and currency values also moved in response to regional economic pressures. Commodity producers faced changing output quotas and legal suspensions.
thread.i: US labor data drove cross-asset repricing as fixed-income markets adjusted to potential Federal Reserve tightening. Central bank policy divergences spurred sharp moves in foreign exchange and equity valuations. Meanwhile, producer group quotas and domestic liquidity measures shaped commodity and banking sectors.
thread.a: US employment prints dictated global rate probabilities and equity momentum. Monetary divergence catalyzed acute forex adjustments, notably through yen carry trade liquidations. Concurrently, targeted fiscal injections and static OPEC+ production quotas anchored regional asset classes.

United States of America.label: United States
United States of America.sub: US payrolls press stocks as yields and inflation loom

stories.t: August Payrolls and Interest Rate Pressures
stories.b: Strong job numbers came out for August. Stock indexes like the S&P 500 and the Dow Jones dropped because of this news. Better jobs data often makes people think the central bank will raise borrowing costs. Higher borrowing costs make stocks less attractive.
stories.i: Hot August payrolls dragged the S&P 500 and the Dow lower. Strong labor data raises expectations that the Federal Reserve might implement further rate hikes. Bond yields reacted to the employment figures, shifting rate probability pricing across portfolios.
stories.a: Robust August payroll prints triggered a repricing of Federal Reserve terminal rate expectations. Equity benchmarks such as the S&P 500 retreated as higher inflation risks and stronger employment reduced the probability of near-term monetary easing. Duration assets felt the pressure immediately as yields climbed.

stories.t: Nasdaq Encounters Resistance Amid Macro Focus
stories.b: The Nasdaq index is hitting its first big test of resistance. Investors are feeling nervous about upcoming consumer price index reports. Geopolitical events in the Middle East are also worrying traders. Growth expectations for the market are starting to look lower.
stories.i: The Nasdaq faces key technical resistance as market uncertainty mounts. Traders are shifting focus toward upcoming consumer price index data releases and ongoing Middle East conflicts. Growth expectations across the technology sector are deteriorating.
stories.a: Technological indices encounter primary resistance levels as macro headwinds intensify. The confluence of upcoming consumer price data and geopolitical friction in the Middle East has compressed valuation multiples. Growth-dependent equities are absorbing downward revisions in earnings expectations.

politics.b: Lawmakers face debates regarding housing tax exclusions and Medicare rules. Citizens deal with social security rules after losing medical certifications. Economic data releases shape the legislative agenda on taxes.
politics.i: Fiscal policy discussions center on capital gains tax exclusions for real estate transactions. Social safety net provisions interact with employment qualifications for aging workers. Regulatory compliance intersects with federal entitlement thresholds.
politics.a: Legislative scrutiny focuses on principal residence tax exclusion limits relative to healthcare financing costs. Labor force participation barriers among older demographics interact with federal disability determinations. Macroeconomic indicators drive fiscal debates surrounding cost-of-living adjustments.

timeline: A residential property was purchased for $62,000.
August payroll figures and consumer price index expectations dominated financial market focus.

United Kingdom.label: United Kingdom
United Kingdom.sub: Design sector growth and bond market shifts

stories.t: Design Sector Expands Across the British Economy
stories.b: The design sector in the UK grew larger than the retail industry. It is now worth £136.7bn. This means the sector generates huge amounts of money for the economy. It forms a massive pillar of financial activity across the country. The data shows how business priorities have shifted toward creative industries.
stories.i: The UK design sector outpaced retail to reach a valuation of £136.7bn. This expansion establishes the industry as a primary pillar of the domestic economy. Creative services now drive substantial commercial output compared to traditional high-street commerce. The milestone reflects changing structural weights within British economic activity.
stories.a: Design sector valuation scaled to £136.7bn, eclipsing retail output to redefine commercial composition. This structural rotation elevates creative industries into a core macroeconomic pillar. Capital allocation within domestic growth metrics now heavily favours intellectual property and design services over traditional consumer goods distribution. The shift alters sectoral output weightings across national accounts.

stories.t: London Stocks Move With Government Bond Yields
stories.b: London stocks slipped because bond yields rose on the first trading day of September. Bond yields are like the interest paid on government loans. Later, the FTSE 100 index rose to 10,831.52. This index tracks the one hundred biggest companies listed in London. A retreat in government bond yields helped lift these rate-sensitive sectors.
stories.i: London stocks slipped initially as government bond yields rose on the first trading day of September. The FTSE 100 subsequently climbed to 10,831.52 as yields retreated. This decline in borrowing costs provided relief to rate-sensitive equities. Market participants adjusted portfolios in response to shifting fixed-income valuations.
stories.a: Equities experienced early downward pressure as sovereign yields climbed during the initial trading session of September. The FTSE 100 subsequently rebounded to 10,831.52 driven by a contraction in government bond yields. This yield compression triggered capital rotation back into rate-sensitive segments. Valuations remain tightly coupled to sovereign debt pricing dynamics.

politics.b: The Chancellor plans to argue that the UK economy can turn a corner. This comes despite recent turmoil in the bond market. Officials face difficult fiscal choices as budget discussions continue.
politics.i: The Chancellor intends to argue that the domestic economy can turn a corner despite ongoing bond market turmoil. Policy discussions centre on fiscal stability amidst shifting market conditions. Financial authorities monitor debt issuance closely.
politics.a: The Chancellor prepares to assert macroeconomic resilience despite severe bond market volatility. Fiscal messaging aims to anchor expectations against sovereign debt repricing risks. Treasury officials navigate borrowing constraints as budgetary pressures mount.

Germany.label: Germany
Germany.sub: German economy faces crisis warnings and central bank rate expectations

stories.t: Stihl Warns of German Economic Crisis
stories.b: Family entrepreneur Stihl warns of a serious crisis in the German economy. The entrepreneur calls for urgent reforms to address the economic problems. Germany faces these warnings while manufacturing and family business leaders speak out about growth. The warnings come from business leaders within the country.
stories.i: Family entrepreneur Stihl warns of a serious crisis in the German economy. The industrial figure calls for urgent reforms to tackle structural hurdles. Germany faces these warnings while manufacturing sectors navigate weakening inflation trends. The calls demand policy changes from regional and federal authorities.
stories.a: Family entrepreneur Stihl warns of a serious crisis in the German economy, demanding urgent structural overhauls. The industrial figure highlights competitiveness losses across key manufacturing verticals. Germany faces these warnings against a backdrop of subdued domestic demand and tight credit. The intervention adds corporate pressure on policymakers ahead of upcoming fiscal decisions.

stories.t: ECB Expected to Raise Rates as Markets Watch DAX
stories.b: The European Central Bank, which sets borrowing costs for countries using the euro, is expected to raise rates. Traders also watch the DAX, which is a stock market index tracking big German companies, as it holds at elevated levels. U.S. inflation data is also in focus for global markets. The European Central Bank decision impacts currency and bond markets.
stories.i: The European Central Bank is expected to raise interest rates this week. Traders monitor the DAX index as it attempts to hold its ground at elevated levels. U.S. inflation data drives broader foreign exchange and bond market moves. The European Central Bank rate action influences currency pairs across the region.
stories.a: The European Central Bank is expected to raise rates in the upcoming policy meeting. The DAX index trades near elevated levels, requiring technical support to maintain momentum. U.S. inflation prints frame the external risk appetite for European equities. The monetary tightening path shapes cross-asset valuations in debt and currency instruments.

politics.b: The AfD won elections in Saxony-Anhalt. The political win is noted by analysts watching German regional politics. Regional elections impact national political discussions.
politics.i: The AfD wins elections in Saxony-Anhalt. The regional vote result draws attention from political analysts monitoring the domestic landscape. The victory shifts local political dynamics in Germany.
politics.a: The AfD wins elections in Saxony-Anhalt, reinforcing its regional electoral footprint. The outcome alters the local legislative balance in Germany. Political analysts evaluate the spillover risks for federal coalition stability.

Japan.label: Japan

stories.t: Yen Surges as Forex Shifts Unwind Trades
stories.b: The Japanese currency jumped by 2.0% recently. This sudden move happened after remarks from a central bank member. Central banks are institutions that manage a country's money supply and interest rates, which are the fees charged for borrowing. These shifts caused investors to unwind a carry trade, where traders borrow cheap money in one place to invest elsewhere. Policy differences between nations drove these global foreign exchange movements.
stories.i: The Japanese currency rallied 2.0% following unexpected remarks from a Bank of Japan official. This sharp appreciation exposed acute market fragility by triggering a rapid unwinding of the yen carry trade. Global forex shifts accelerated as traders reacted to ongoing policy divergence between Tokyo and other major central banks.
stories.a: Spot appreciation of 2.0% in the Japanese currency triggered systemic liquidations via the carry trade channel following hawkish Bank of Japan commentary. The abrupt reversal highlights latent market fragility as cross-border positioning unravels. Macro divergence continues to dictate foreign exchange adjustments across global desks.

stories.t: Budget Requests Climb to Pandemic Scale
stories.b: Government budget requests in Japan swelled to pandemic-era levels. These spending plans emerged under Takaichi. Public spending impacts the broader economy by increasing demand for goods and services. Ministries submitted large financial requirements for review.
stories.i: Official fiscal demands from Japanese ministries expanded to pandemic-era scales under Takaichi. The elevated spending requests reflect broad departmental requirements submitted for the upcoming fiscal cycle. Government outlays of this magnitude typically influence domestic debt issuance plans.
stories.a: Fiscal expenditure requests scaled to pandemic-era baselines under Takaichi. Ministry-level submissions indicate aggressive resource claims ahead of formal cabinet consolidation. The magnitude of these appropriations directly influences primary deficit projections and sovereign debt supply dynamics.

politics.b: Political figures in Japan are overseeing massive budget demands that match the spending seen during the global pandemic. These funding requirements come from various government ministries. Leaders must now evaluate these large figures against the financial health of the nation.
politics.i: Japanese policymakers face expansive fiscal demands as ministry budget requests reach pandemic-era proportions under Takaichi. The political administration must balance these large expenditure targets against sovereign debt constraints. Administrative reviews will determine which projects receive official funding.
politics.a: The Takaichi administration confronts substantial fiscal expansion as ministerial budget applications scale to pandemic-era highs. Executive oversight will dictate the degree of budgetary consolidation applied to these competing departmental demands. Legislative negotiations will subsequently shape the final fiscal package.

timeline: Yen jumps 2% following remarks from a Bank of Japan member.
Japan budget requests swell to pandemic-era scale under Takaichi.

China.label: China
China.sub: China injects billions into banks and insurers

stories.t: China Pours Billions Into Financial Sector
stories.b: The Chinese government injected $54 billion into state banks and insurers. Banks are businesses where people keep their money and get loans. This injection helps these financial institutions strengthen their balance sheets. Officials want the capital boost to support economic growth. The stimulus package targets sluggish growth conditions.
stories.i: State authorities injected $54 billion into major lenders and insurers to bolster capital adequacy. The capital injection aims to offset deflationary pressures and sluggish economic momentum. Regulators designed the measure to enable these institutions to extend further credit. The recapitalisation targets the financial core to stimulate broader commercial activity.
stories.a: State authorities deployed a $54 billion recapitalisation targeting systemic lenders and insurers to mitigate deflationary headwinds. The transmission channel relies on expanding Tier 1 capital buffers to override risk aversion in credit creation. This sovereign backstop implies policymakers are prioritizing balance-sheet repair over organic deleveraging. The efficacy of the stimulus depends on whether loan demand responds to the augmented lending capacity.

politics.b: Authorities in China announced a large financial package to support banks and insurers. Officials want to fix sluggish growth across the country. The funding totals $54 billion.
politics.i: Beijing announced a $54 billion recapitalisation package for state banks and insurers. The policy intervention addresses persistent economic sluggishness. Authorities deployed the funds to reinforce the financial sector.
politics.a: State organs authorized a $54 billion capital injection into systemic financial institutions. The fiscal intervention responds directly to macroeconomic deceleration. Policymakers directed the funds toward state lenders and insurers.

timeline: China announced a $54 billion capital boost for state banks and insurers.

India.label: India
India.sub: Reserve Bank holds interest rate and forecasts GDP

stories.t: Interest Rates and Economic Growth Projections
stories.b: The Reserve Bank of India is the main bank that sets financial rules for the country. It decided to keep its repo rate, which is the interest rate it charges other banks for loans, exactly the same. At the same time, the central bank calculated that the country's real gross domestic product, meaning the total value of all goods and services produced after removing price changes, will grow by 6.9% during the current fiscal year.
stories.i: The Reserve Bank of India left its repo rate unchanged. Alongside this monetary policy decision, the central bank projected that the country's real GDP growth for the current fiscal year will reach 6.9%.
stories.a: The Reserve Bank of India maintained the repo rate at its existing level while publishing a real GDP growth projection of 6.9% for the current fiscal year. This macroeconomic guidance anchors local yield curves while market participants parse the central bank's stance on domestic demand resilience.

stories.t: Mutual Fund Retail and High Net Worth Participation
stories.b: Ordinary retail investors are putting a smaller share of their money into mutual funds for the second year in a row. Meanwhile, high net worth individuals, who are very wealthy people with large amounts of cash to invest, are increasing their financial bets in this area. This shift changes who owns the overall pool of mutual fund assets in the market.
stories.i: Retail share in the mutual fund pie shrank for the second consecutive year. In contrast, high net worth individuals ramped up their bets in the sector, altering asset distribution.
stories.a: Retail participation in mutual fund assets contracted for a second straight year. Simultaneously, high net worth individuals scaled up allocations, modifying the underlying liquidity profile of the domestic asset management industry.

politics.b: The regulatory authorities announced new security rules to stop digital financial scams. Government leaders continue to monitor financial stability.
politics.i: The Reserve Bank of India proposed new safety protocols to combat digital financial fraud. Regulatory bodies maintain oversight over domestic transaction security.
politics.a: The Reserve Bank of India formulated updated safety measures aimed at mitigating digital fraud vectors across payment systems. Regulatory oversight remains focused on systemic operational resilience.

timeline: Reserve Bank of India keeps repo rate unchanged and forecasts 6.9% GDP growth.
Data shows retail share in mutual funds shrinking for the second consecutive year.
Reserve Bank of India proposes new safety measures against digital frauds.

Brazil.label: Brazil
Brazil.sub: Sigma Lithium mine suspension and Petrobras deals

stories.t: Sigma Lithium Mine Operations Suspended by Court
stories.b: A court in Brazil ordered a halt to work at the only mine run by Sigma Lithium. This company trades its shares on the Nasdaq stock market in the United States under the ticker SGML. The stoppage impacts all production at that sole site.
stories.i: A Brazilian court suspended operations at Sigma Lithium's sole producing mine, which trades under the ticker SGML on the Nasdaq. The injunction halts active extraction at the company's primary asset.
stories.a: A Brazilian judicial body suspended operations at Sigma Lithium's sole producing asset, SGML on the Nasdaq, halting output entirely. The court order halts cash flow from the company's primary revenue-generating facility.

stories.t: Oil States Secures Petrobras Maintenance Contract
stories.b: Oil States Brasil won a three-year contract from Petrobras. Petrobras is a major Brazilian state-backed oil company. The deal covers subsea maintenance and support work.
stories.i: Oil States Brasil secured a three-year subsea maintenance and support agreement with Petrobras. The contract extends the supplier's operational footprint with the state-controlled energy producer.
stories.a: Oil States Brasil secured a three-year subsea maintenance and support contract with Petroleo Brasileiro SA. The award formalises an extended service relationship for offshore infrastructure upkeep.

politics.b: Legal decisions in Brazil can instantly halt major mining operations, while state-backed energy firms continue awarding large supply contracts.
politics.i: Judicial interventions continue to create operational risk for resource extractors in Brazil, contrasting with steady procurement activity by state-controlled Petrobras.
politics.a: Regulatory and judicial headwinds for independent miners in Brazil contrast with ongoing state-backed procurement pipelines in the offshore oil sector.

timeline: Oil States Brasil wins a three-year Petrobras subsea maintenance contract.
A Brazilian court suspends operations at Sigma Lithium's sole producing mine.

Saudi Arabia.label: Saudi Arabia
Saudi Arabia.sub: OPEC+ output policy and Aramco gas development

stories.t: OPEC+ Keeps October Production Quotas Unchanged
stories.b: OPEC+, a big group of countries that sell oil, decided not to change how much oil they pump. They paused plans to increase their oil output. The group kept their production levels the same for October. This choice comes as oil prices settle slightly higher.
stories.i: OPEC+ maintained its October production level and halted its planned output hike. The producer group kept quotas steady amid broader market monitoring of US inflation figures. Oil prices settled slightly higher following the decision.
stories.a: OPEC+ preserved output targets for October, foregoing scheduled production increases as member states navigate demand signals. The supply hold coincides with markets weighing macroeconomic prints against ongoing geopolitical risks in the Middle East. Crude benchmarks edged higher in response to the static supply trajectory.

stories.t: Saudi Aramco Pursues Arabian Desert Shale Gas
stories.b: Saudi Aramco started a new project to find shale gas in the Arabian Desert. People call this a shale gas revolution. The company wants to bring new gas methods to the desert. Saudi Aramco previously set earnings records that tech firms like Nvidia now target.
stories.i: Saudi Aramco initiated a shale gas development strategy across the Arabian Desert. The national oil company applies unconventional extraction techniques to tap domestic reserves. Nvidia net income projections now approach historical benchmarks previously set by Aramco.
stories.a: Saudi Aramco introduced unconventional drilling operations to the Arabian Desert to expand domestic gas feedstock. The engineering push targets shale formations to diversify local energy supplies. Meanwhile, enterprise equity valuations project peer tech earnings to challenge Aramco's historical net income peak by 2029.

politics.b: The Council of Economic and Development Affairs met to talk about the Saudi economy and Vision 2030. Vision 2030 is a big government plan for the country. Ministers reviewed current economic goals.
politics.i: The Council of Economic and Development Affairs reviewed domestic economic progress and Vision 2030 initiatives. Ministers evaluated ongoing development benchmarks. The state continues to manage strategic diversification projects.
politics.a: The Council of Economic and Development Affairs convened to audit domestic reform milestones tied to Vision 2030. Officials assessed macroeconomic indicators alongside structural diversification metrics. The administrative review underscores policy alignment with long-term industrial transition targets.

timeline: OPEC+ decided to keep October production quotas steady.

Nigeria.label: Nigeria
Nigeria.sub: Foreign reserves top $54bn as naira gains and OPEC holds

stories.t: Nigerian Currency and Foreign Reserves Rise
stories.b: Foreign reserves are the money a country keeps in foreign currencies to pay for imports. Nigeria's foreign reserves climbed past $54bn. The Nigerian naira gained N8.21 against the US dollar during the first week of September. This means the local currency bought slightly more foreign money than before.
stories.i: Nigeria's foreign reserves grew past $54bn. The naira climbed by N8.21 against the dollar across the first week of September. Higher reserve cushions typically alter liquidity conditions in the foreign exchange market.
stories.a: Foreign reserves surpassed $54bn, coinciding with the naira appreciating by N8.21 against the dollar in the first week of September. This reserve accumulation expands central bank intervention capacity in the foreign exchange market. The sustainability of this appreciation depends on portfolio inflows and hydrocarbon export receipts.

stories.t: OPEC Maintains Output Quotas for October
stories.b: OPEC is a group of countries that produce oil. They decide together how much oil to pump out each day. OPEC and its partners decided to keep their production quotas unchanged for October. Nigeria wanted to produce more oil than its current limit allows.
stories.i: OPEC and its allies kept production quotas unchanged for October. Nigeria sought a higher production limit during the talks. Production caps restrict the volume of crude oil the country can legally pump to generate export revenue.
stories.a: OPEC maintained its production quota unchanged for October. Nigeria pursued a higher production baseline during the ministerial discussions. The restriction constrains fiscal revenue expansion tied to crude extraction volumes.

stories.t: Nigerian Stocks Rise on FTSE Return
stories.b: Stocks are small pieces of ownership in companies that people buy and sell on an exchange. Nigerian stocks gained 2.36%. This increase happened because the FTSE index returned to the market, which drove up buying.
stories.i: Nigerian equities advanced by 2.36%. The return of the FTSE index drove buying activity across the exchange. Index inclusion mechanics prompted portfolio rebalancing into local listings.
stories.a: Nigerian equities appreciated by 2.36%. The return of the FTSE index catalyzed the buying momentum. Passive and active fund rebalancing following the index readmission drove the capital inflows.

politics.b: Political figures discussed economic plans and spending audits. The APC party shared a roadmap aimed at building a $1tn economy. At the same time, critics and rival politicians called for investigations into missing welfare funds.
politics.i: The APC unveiled a roadmap targeting a $1tn economy under Tinubu. Meanwhile, political pressure mounted over alleged mismanaged welfare funds. SERAP and opposition figures demanded investigations into billions of naira in poverty alleviation allocations.
politics.a: The APC released a policy framework targeting a $1tn economic valuation under Tinubu. Concurrently, governance scrutiny intensified regarding alleged diversion of poverty intervention funds. SERAP and opposition figures demanded formal anti-corruption inquiries into multi-billion naira disbursement discrepancies.

timeline: Foreign reserves top $54bn and the naira gains N8.21 against the dollar

Australia.label: Australia
Australia.sub: ASX futures flat as US payrolls and Middle East tensions weigh

stories.t: Australian Market Opens Flat Following US Payroll Data
stories.b: The Australian stock market got ready to open flat on Monday. Overseas markets dropped after a very strong US jobs report came out for August. Traders worried that the Federal Reserve, which is the central bank of the United States that sets borrowing costs, might raise interest rates higher. ASX 200 futures pointed to a flat start for local trading.
stories.i: Australian shares faced a cautious start as S&P 500 and Dow indices declined. Hot US August payroll figures drove up expectations for additional monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve. ASX 200 futures remained flat during early morning trading sessions.
stories.a: ASX 200 futures opened flat while offshore equities absorbed the macroeconomic shock of hot August US non-farm payrolls. Elevated employment prints shifted terminal rate pricing upward, compressing risk assets globally. The domestic session commenced against this restrictive liquidity backdrop.

stories.t: Geopolitical Pressures and Corporate Valuations Face ASX Traders
stories.b: The local share market also reacted to a growing war involving Iran. Investors checked company values for firms like Flight Centre Travel Group and Domino's. Domino's reported wider losses while altering its dividend payout. Joyce Corporation approached its ex-dividend date while other large companies experienced heavy losses.
stories.i: The local benchmark faced sentiment pressures as the conflict involving Iran escalated. Corporate valuations drew intense scrutiny across the ASX following earnings and dividend announcements from firms such as Flight Centre Travel Group and Domino's. Domino's adjusted its dividend structure amid expanding corporate losses.
stories.a: Geopolitical risk premium expanded across the local board as the Iran war escalated. Equity analysts re-evaluated corporate valuations for Flight Centre Travel Group and Domino's following divergent earnings and dividend disclosures. Domino's recalibrated capital return policies despite widening bottom-line deficits.

politics.b: Global political tensions rose as the war involving Iran escalated. Overseas economic data from the United States shifted market expectations. Australian markets monitored these international events closely.
politics.i: Escalating conflict involving Iran introduced geopolitical risk to the ASX opening. Macroeconomic releases from the United States dominated international investor sentiment.
politics.a: Cross-border risk transmission channels amplified as the Iran conflict intensified. External macroeconomic surprises from the United States dictated domestic risk appetite.

timeline: ASX 200 futures indicated a flat open following US payroll figures.
